I'm designing a motion/"juice" system (animations, shader accents, interaction variants) for Twyne, a Qwik + TipTap/ProseMirror local-first writing app at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne. Brand: editorial, letterpress, literary writer's room (paper, ink, stamps, vermilion/cobalt). I need a precise inventory of the **manuscript text surface** — what happens as the writer types, moves the mouse, selects, scrolls, and drags — so I can add identity-carrying motion without harming writing. Do not edit anything.

Scope:
- `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx` (4700 lines — grep, don't read whole): extension list, caret/gapcursor, onUpdate scheduling (scheduleLiveMeta / scheduleDerive), drag and drop handling (files, blocks, images), paste, pointer handlers, comment/citation/suggestion marks and how they are clicked, the selection popover, zen mode CSS (around line 450), the `.twyne-mark-anchor` chips.
- `src/components/editor/extensions/*` (list each extension and what it decorates), `manuscript-panel.tsx`, `selection-actions.tsx`, `slash-command-menu.tsx`, `suggestion-panel.tsx`, `user-comment-panel.tsx`, `persona-note-panel.tsx`, `find-replace-panel.tsx`, `grammar-panel.tsx`, `document-outline.tsx`, `image-inspector.tsx`, `floating-table-toolbar.tsx`, `insert-panels.tsx`, `forecast-line.tsx`.
- `src/components/in-flow/*` (flow-surface, flow-ribbon, margin-rail, passage-gather, sentence-bench, thread-instrument, tool-renderer): what "flow" states exist (`data-flow`), how typing-vs-idle is detected, what appears in the margins.
- Relevant global.css rules (src/global.css is 10k lines — grep: `.ProseMirror`, `.page-canvas`, `.manuscript-scroller`, `.twyne-comment-mark`, `.citation-mark`, `.drag-overlay`, `twyne-gapcursor`, `selection`, `::selection`, `caret-color`, `.zen-mode`).

For EACH component/sub-element report compactly:
1. file:line, what it shows.
2. Triggers: typing, caret move, selection, hover, click, scroll, drag, keyboard.
3. Current feedback/motion (class names, keyframes, global.css line numbers), and busy/error/success variants.
4. Consequence class of actions: local-only edit, sends text to an AI provider / spends hosted credits, syncs/collab, destructive.
5. Performance-sensitive paths (anything that runs per keystroke; whether decorations re-render; IME/composition handling).

Also answer specifically: Is there a custom caret? Does anything track scroll position (scroll listeners, IntersectionObserver)? Is there paragraph drag-handle reordering? What is the CSS for `::selection` and caret-color? What fonts/colours does the page use?

Return a structured, terse list with file:line references. Under ~1500 words.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
